main_body: Flat grass ground patch, 4x3 tiles, a uniform green field with scattered lighter and darker pixel clumps; no standing volume.
evidence: The candidate is a ground texture tile with no vertical object. The 3/4 contract (top band + front face) does not apply to terrain. It is a seamless grass pattern with repeating tufts, so there is no projection fault such as a front elevation, side elevation or top-down slab of an object. It is judged as valid terrain.

style.evidence: The grass uses a mid green base with light and dark green tuft clusters (about 4 steps: light, light-mid, base, dark). The tufts repeat in the same pattern every 16px, which makes it read as a tiled stamp, and the base fill between tufts is a large flat area of one colour with little grain. The Beodeul grass reference has more varied tufts and more tonal steps. There are no outlines, which is fine for grass. It is a bit thinner and flatter than the reference, with low per-tile colour count in the empty areas of each tile.
